verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's own CKS product provides managed Kubernetes clusters on bare metal that you control with kubectl, which implies you can deploy workloads from your own container images, though no doc explicitly says so. Node Pools share a common configuration, but only labels, taints, and annotations are documented, not custom OS or machine images. missing for 10: explicit documentation of running custom Docker or container images, custom node or machine image templates, private registry support, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
